jp: 棚[たな]にかばんが五[いつ]つあります。田中[たなか]さんのかばんは{どれ|ko-dore}ですか。
en: There are five bags on the shelf. Which one is Mr. Tanaka's bag?
why: Choosing one from several known things, with no noun after it, is どれ.

jp: このメニューの中[なか]で、{どれ|ko-dore}が一番[いちばん]人気[にんき]ですか。
en: Which of the items on this menu is the most popular?
why: Picking one out of a list of three or more things, with no noun directly after, is どれ.

jp: ケーキが六[むっ]つあります。{どれ|ko-dore}を食[た]べますか。
en: There are six cakes. Which one will you eat?
why: The blank stands alone as the pronoun "which one" among many, so it is どれ.

jp: シャツが五枚[ごまい]あります。一番[いちばん]小[ちい]さいのは{どれ|ko-dore}ですか。
en: There are five shirts. Which one is the smallest?
why: A pronoun asking which one among several things in view is どれ.

jp: 先生[せんせい]、この四[よっ]つの中[なか]で{どれ|ko-dore}が正[ただ]しい答[こた]えですか。
en: Teacher, which of these four is the correct answer?
why: The choice is among several listed answers and no noun follows, so どれ.

jp: 鍵[かぎ]がたくさんありますね。玄関[げんかん]の鍵[かぎ]は{どれ|ko-dore}ですか。
en: There are lots of keys. Which one is the key to the front door?
why: Singling out one item from a large group is どれ; two would be どちら.

jp: あそこに自転車[じてんしゃ]が十台[じゅうだい]ぐらいあります。山田[やまだ]さんのは{どれ|ko-dore}ですか。
en: There are about ten bicycles over there. Which one is Ms. Yamada's?
why: One bicycle out of about ten is どれ, a pronoun with no following noun.

jp: 新[あたら]しい携帯[けいたい]が三台[さんだい]出[で]ました。{どれ|ko-dore}を買[か]うつもりですか。
en: Three new phones have come out. Which one do you plan to buy?
why: Choosing among three things and acting on it with を directly is どれ.

jp: このお菓子[かし]は全部[ぜんぶ]おいしそうですね。{どれ|ko-dore}にしようかな。
en: These sweets all look delicious. Which one shall I pick?
why: A pronoun for one choice out of many sweets is どれ; there is no noun after the blank.

jp: ここにある辞書[じしょ]の中[なか]で、{どれ|ko-dore}が一番[いちばん]使[つか]いやすいですか。
en: Of the dictionaries here, which is the easiest to use?
why: The set has three or more members and the blank stands alone, so どれ.

jp: リモコンにボタンがいくつかあります。エアコンをつけるのは{どれ|ko-dore}ですか。
en: The remote has several buttons. Which one turns on the air conditioner?
why: Picking one button out of several is どれ, used as a noun.

jp: 机[つくえ]の上[うえ]にかばんが三[みっ]つあります。{どの|ko-dore}かばんがあなたのですか。
en: There are three bags on the desk. Which bag is yours?
why: The blank comes directly before the noun かばん, and どの modifies a noun.

jp: {どの|ko-dore}電車[でんしゃ]に乗[の]れば、空港[くうこう]に行[い]けますか。
en: Which train should I take to get to the airport?
why: "Which" directly before a noun (電車) is どの; どれ cannot take a noun.

jp: {どの|ko-dore}先生[せんせい]が山田[やまだ]先生[せんせい]ですか。
en: Which teacher is Mr. Yamada?
why: どの attaches straight to the noun 先生 to ask which one.

jp: あなたは{どの|ko-dore}季節[きせつ]が一番[いちばん]好[す]きですか。
en: Which season do you like best?
why: Choosing among the four seasons before a noun is どの; どんな would ask for a description.

jp: {どの|ko-dore}道[みち]を行[い]けば、駅[えき]に着[つ]きますか。
en: Which road leads to the station?
why: "Which" + noun (道) is どの; どれ and どちら cannot be followed directly by a noun.

jp: このクラスでは、{どの|ko-dore}学生[がくせい]が一番[いちばん]背[せ]が高[たか]いですか。
en: In this class, which student is the tallest?
why: A known group of students and a noun right after the blank call for どの.

jp: {どの|ko-dore}店[みせ]で昼[ひる]ご飯[はん]を食[た]べましょうか。
en: Which restaurant shall we have lunch at?
why: Asking which of the known candidate restaurants, with 店 following, is どの.

jp: 写真[しゃしん]の中[なか]の{どの|ko-dore}人[ひと]が、あなたのお兄[にい]さんですか。
en: Which person in the photo is your older brother?
why: Picking one person out of a photo, with the noun 人 after it, is どの.

jp: 店[みせ]にはセーターが十着[じゅっちゃく]ありました。{どの|ko-dore}セーターを買[か]いましたか。
en: The shop had ten sweaters. Which sweater did you buy?
why: The blank modifies セーター and asks which one of a known set, so どの.

jp: {どの|ko-dore}バスが市役所[しやくしょ]へ行[い]きますか。
en: Which bus goes to the city hall?
why: "Which" + noun (バス) is どの, not a stand-alone どれ.

jp: あなたは{どの|ko-dore}国[くに]から来[き]ましたか。
en: Which country did you come from?
why: Asking which country, with 国 right after the blank, takes どの.

jp: 三冊[さんさつ]読[よ]みましたね。{どの|ko-dore}本[ほん]が一番[いちばん]面白[おもしろ]かったですか。
en: You read three books. Which book was the most interesting?
why: The choice is among the three books just mentioned, and 本 follows, so どの.

jp: コーヒーと紅茶[こうちゃ]、{どちら|ko-dore}がいいですか。
en: Coffee or tea: which would you like?
why: There are exactly two choices, so "which of the two" is どちら.

jp: すみません、駅[えき]は{どちら|ko-dore}ですか。
en: Excuse me, which way is the station?
why: Politely asking the direction or location of a place is どちら.

jp: お国[くに]は{どちら|ko-dore}ですか。
en: Which country are you from? (polite)
why: The polite way to ask someone's home country or place is どちら.

jp: お兄[にい]さんと弟[おとうと]さんの{どちら|ko-dore}が背[せ]が高[たか]いですか。
en: Which is taller, your older brother or your younger brother?
why: Comparing exactly two people (the two brothers) takes どちら.

jp: 右[みぎ]と左[ひだり]の{どちら|ko-dore}に曲[ま]がりますか。
en: Which way will you turn, right or left?
why: Right and left are the only two options, so どちら.

jp: 夏休[なつやす]みは、海[うみ]と山[やま]の{どちら|ko-dore}に行[い]きたいですか。
en: For the summer holidays, which do you want to go to, the sea or the mountains?
why: There are exactly two places to choose between, so どちら.

jp: 電話[でんわ]で：失礼[しつれい]ですが、{どちら|ko-dore}様[さま]ですか。
en: On the phone: Excuse me, who is calling, please?
why: The polite form for asking who someone is, before 様, is どちら.

jp: トイレは{どちら|ko-dore}にありますか。
en: Where is the restroom? (polite)
why: A polite question about where something is uses どちら.

jp: 肉[にく]と魚[さかな]、{どちら|ko-dore}の方[ほう]が好[す]きですか。
en: Meat or fish: which do you like better?
why: Two things are compared, and the pattern どちらの方が asks which of the two.

jp: このシャツとあのシャツでは、{どちら|ko-dore}が安[やす]いですか。
en: Between this shirt and that shirt, which is cheaper?
why: Only two shirts are compared, so どちら.

jp: バスと電車[でんしゃ]では、{どちら|ko-dore}が速[はや]いですか。
en: Which is faster, the bus or the train?
why: A comparison of exactly two means of transport takes どちら.

jp: あなたは{どんな|ko-dore}音楽[おんがく]が好[す]きですか。
en: What kind of music do you like?
why: The question asks for the type or kind of music, which is どんな.

jp: {どんな|ko-dore}仕事[しごと]をしたいですか。
en: What kind of work do you want to do?
why: Asking about the kind of work, not one of a set, takes どんな.

jp: 昨日[きのう]は{どんな|ko-dore}映画[えいが]を見[み]ましたか。
en: What kind of movie did you see yesterday?
why: The speaker asks about the genre or nature of the film, so どんな.

jp: 新[あたら]しい先生[せんせい]は、{どんな|ko-dore}人[ひと]ですか。
en: What kind of person is the new teacher?
why: Asking about someone's character or type takes どんな.

jp: {どんな|ko-dore}食[た]べ物[もの]が苦手[にがて]ですか。
en: What kinds of food do you dislike?
why: The question asks what kind of food, not which item of a set, so どんな.

jp: {どんな|ko-dore}部屋[へや]を探[さが]していますか。
en: What kind of room are you looking for?
why: Asking for the features or type of a room is どんな.

jp: 京都[きょうと]は{どんな|ko-dore}町[まち]ですか。
en: What kind of city is Kyoto?
why: Describing the nature of a city is asked with どんな.

jp: {どんな|ko-dore}スポーツをよくしますか。
en: What kind of sports do you often play?
why: The question asks for the kind of sport, so どんな.

jp: {どんな|ko-dore}色[いろ]が好[す]きですか。
en: What kind of colours do you like?
why: Asking about a kind or type (here colour) in general is どんな.

jp: あなたの国[くに]の夏[なつ]は、{どんな|ko-dore}天気[てんき]ですか。
en: What is the weather like in summer in your country?
why: Asking what the weather is like, a description, takes どんな.

jp: 最近[さいきん]{どんな|ko-dore}本[ほん]を読[よ]んでいますか。
en: What kind of books have you been reading lately?
why: Asking about the kind of books read in general is どんな.

jp: {どんな|ko-dore}家[いえ]に住[す]みたいですか。
en: What kind of house do you want to live in?
why: The question asks for the type of house wanted, so どんな.
